long_biography.plain_text:
Property businessman Alan Chuang developed his knowledge of Chinese porcelain through study, auctions and business trips to Beijing. His first auction purchase was a famille-rose vase in 1981. Over subsequent decades he assembled imperial ceramics spanning the Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties, with a taste for finely worked vases and cups.

His collection became the subject of a bilingual catalogue by ceramics specialist Julian Thompson, with advice from other Chinese-art experts. A later dedicated auction presented small-scale works from the collection, including a set of twelve Kangxi cups decorated with flowers associated with the months of the year.
